request: Prepare a fair-test planning lesson for ball surface finish. Students should critique the old records and specify allocation, controls, measurement and a blank results table without predicting an effect.
objective: Control release position while comparing surface finishes with independent balls and a defined stopping-distance measure.

sources.text: Fictional tabletop track log: polished balls released at mark H travelled a median of95cm along the level section; rough-finish balls released at mark L travelled65cm. H andL are different starting heights. The number of balls and individual distances are missing.

Thirty identical unfinished model balls are available. Either surface finish can be applied to each while retaining the stated target mass and diameter; each ball is used for its first roll only. Both finishes can be released at either mark. Keep track, level surface and release gate identical.

Measure from the ramp exit line to the front edge of the ball when it first remains still for two seconds. Record ball ID, finish, mark, order and distance. If a ball leaves the track, record the event rather than selecting a better second run. No new trials have been run.
